pack: EchoAural Meter Master – Exam-Style Complementary Bank
notes: This bank is designed to be used alongside the original exact-time-signature questions.
Each existing MTR audio clip is used by two complementary exam-style questions.
Thirty questions are listening-only; thirty require a score crop from the existing linked public-domain score.
Score assets are not included and must be created using the instructions and public-domain score links.
MMX061 reuses the existing Texture Trainer TT097 audio asset without duplicating the MP3.

MMX063-MMX100: 38 CIE (Cambridge IGCSE Music 0410)-style questions added 2026-08-12 from the "GOOD MORNIN JIMMY WORK!" real-audio candidate batch (meter-master-new-50.json), after user review (31 kept as-is, 7 edited per review notes; 11 dropped; 1 routed to Instrument Identifier as II376).

2026-08-12 (second review pass, original MMX001-061 bank): user reviewed all 61 original exam-style questions via modules/meter-master/review.html. 17 dropped (MMX008,010,019,020,027,038,043,046,047,048,050,053,054,055,058,059,060). MMX029 converted from a 2-mark written 'describe the metre' question to a 1-mark multiple-choice 'how many beats are in each bar?' question (options 2/3/4/5, answer 5). 12 score-based questions (MMX032,033,034,035,036,039,041,044,045,049,051,056) standardised into the 'Skeleton-score completion' format ("The time signature has been removed from the score. Write the missing time signature. (1)", 4-option multiple choice, Pearson Edexcel board style, 1 mark) per review notes, and script.js's deriveQuestionLevel was updated so this specific score+mode combination now resolves to Developing (previously any score question was hard-coded to Securing). MMX040 (also score, also 'Rhythm and metre features' mode) was explicitly excluded from this conversion per its own review note (compound metre, kept in its original 2-mark written format).

questions.question: A dumka is a Slavic genre built from two contrasting types of section. Which best describes them? (1)
options: A slow, melancholic section alternating with a faster, dance-like section
Two equally fast sections in different keys
A single continuous tempo with no contrast
A slow introduction followed by one fast section with no return
questions.correct_answer: a slow, melancholic section alternating with a faster, dance-like section
accepted_answers: slow melancholic alternating with faster dance like section
questions.mark_scheme: A slow, melancholic section alternating with a faster, dance-like section. (1)

questions.question: In a dumka movement, does the character (tempo and mood) typically stay the same throughout, or change between sections? Name the two contrasting section types. (2)

It stays the same — always fast and lively
It stays the same — always slow and mournful
It changes — loud and soft sections only

questions.mark_scheme: It changes / alternates. (1) Between a slow, melancholic (lament-like) section and a faster, dance-like section. (1)
questions.feedback: Unlike a typical minuet or scherzo, a dumka's character changes repeatedly, alternating slow lament-like music with faster dance-like music.
